body.zh-Hant: 德國國家圖書館權威檔記載，伊斯梅爾·蒙特斯生於1861年10月5日，出生地是玻利維亞拉巴斯帕卡赫斯省的科羅科羅，卒於1933年10月16日，卒地為拉巴斯。美國國會圖書館人名權威檔以「Montes, Ismael, 1861-1933」為正式款目，並收有「Montes Gamboa」的異寫。
body.en: The German National Library authority record gives Ismael Montes's birth on 5 October 1861 at Coro Coro (Pacajes province, La Paz, Bolivia) and his death on 16 October 1933 in La Paz. The Library of Congress name authority uses "Montes, Ismael, 1861-1933" as the heading and lists the variant "Montes Gamboa".

citations.quote: Coro Coro (La Paz, Provinz Pacajes, Bolivien)

body.zh-Hant: 權威檔記他曾兩度擔任玻利維亞總統，第一任從1904年8月14日到1909年8月12日。另一筆權威記錄顯示，瓦倫廷·阿貝西亞（Valentín Abecia）在蒙特斯的第一屆政府中擔任副總統。
body.en: The authority record says he was twice President of Bolivia, the first time from 14 August 1904 to 12 August 1909. Another authority record shows that Valentín Abecia served as vice president in Montes's first government.

citations.quote: Vizepräsident Boliviens in der ersten Regierung Ismael Montes Gamboa

body.zh-Hant: 他第二任總統任期從1913年8月14日到1917年8月15日。權威檔的職業欄除總統與政治人物外，還列有軍人與外交官。
body.en: His second presidency ran from 14 August 1913 to 15 August 1917. Besides president and politician, the authority record lists soldier and diplomat among his occupations.

body.zh-Hant: 權威檔註記他1919年以外交官身分活動，並收有冠以「將軍」稱號的異稱款目。
body.en: The authority record notes diplomatic activity in 1919 and carries a variant heading with the title "General".

body.zh-Hant: 柯立芝生於1872年，出生地是佛蒙特州的普利茅斯諾奇，幼時幫開店的父親記帳。他於1895年以優等成績自阿默斯特學院畢業，1897年夏天通過律師考試，隨後開設律師事務所。
body.en: Coolidge was born in 1872 in Plymouth Notch, Vermont, and grew up helping his storekeeper father keep accounts. He graduated from Amherst College with honors in 1895, passed the bar in the summer of 1897, and then opened a law office.

citations.quote: born John Calvin Coolidge on July 4, 1872, in Plymouth Notch, Vermont
helping his storekeeper father tend accounts
obtain entry to the prestigious Amherst College
passing the bar in the summer of 1897
He then opened a law office

body.zh-Hant: 柯立芝1910年被北安普敦市民選為市長，1912年贏得全州選舉進入麻州參議院，1914年擔任參議院議長。德國國家圖書館權威檔記他1916至1919年任副州長、1919至1921年任麻薩諸塞州州長。任州長期間，他出動州國民兵制止波士頓警察罷工，因而受到全國關注。
body.en: In 1910 the citizens of Northampton selected Coolidge as mayor; in 1912 he won a statewide race for the Massachusetts Senate and in 1914 served as its president. The German National Library authority record gives 1916–1919 as lieutenant governor and 1919–1921 as governor of Massachusetts. As governor he called out the state National Guard to break a strike by Boston police, which brought him national attention.

citations.quote: In 1910, the citizens of Northampton selected him as their mayor
he won a statewide race for the Massachusetts Senate in 1912
he called out the state's National Guard to break a strike by Boston city police

body.zh-Hant: 權威檔記柯立芝1921至1923年任美國副總統。米勒中心的專文說，他任副總統時在哈定政府中作用不大。1923年8月2日，柯立芝的父親叫醒正在度假的他，告知哈定因心臟病發作去世；父親以治安法官身分為他宣誓，他成為第30任總統。
body.en: The authority record gives Coolidge's vice presidency as 1921–1923. The Miller Center essay says he played little role in the Harding administration. On 2 August 1923 Coolidge's father woke his vacationing son to tell him of Harding's death from a heart attack; the father, a justice of the peace, administered the oath of office, and Coolidge became the 30th President.

citations.quote: As vice president, Coolidge played little role in the Harding administration
On August 2, 1923, John Coolidge woke his vacationing son
President Harding's death from a heart attack
the elder Coolidge, a justice of the peace, administered the oath of office
as the 30th President of the United States

body.zh-Hant: 1924年柯立芝贏得共和黨提名並在大選中獲54%選票，共和黨的競選口號是「與柯立芝一起保持冷靜」。權威檔記他任總統至1929年。1927年夏天度假時，他以手寫字條向記者宣布「我不打算在1928年競選總統」。
body.en: In 1924 Coolidge won the Republican nomination and took 54 percent of the vote under the Republican slogan "Keep Cool with Coolidge". The authority record says he governed until 1929. On his summer vacation in 1927 he told reporters in a handwritten note that he did not choose to run for President in 1928.

citations.quote: Coolidge won 54 percent of the vote
urged the nation to "Keep Cool with Coolidge," a popular slogan
In der Präsidentschaftswahl 1924 bestätigt regierte er bis 1929
I do not choose to run for President in 1928.
handwritten strips of paper to reporters

body.zh-Hant: 卸任後柯立芝回到麻薩諸塞州北安普敦，寫作自傳與雜誌文章。1933年1月5日午餐後，他在臥室昏倒，夫人發現他因冠狀動脈血栓而去世；德國國家圖書館權威檔同樣記他卒於1933年1月5日，卒地北安普敦。
body.en: After leaving office Coolidge returned to Northampton, Massachusetts, and wrote his autobiography and magazine articles. On 5 January 1933, just after lunch, he collapsed in his bedroom and his wife found him dead of coronary thrombosis; the German National Library record likewise gives his death as 5 January 1933 in Northampton.

citations.quote: writing his autobiography and articles for national magazines
On January 5, 1933, just after lunch, Coolidge collapsed in his bedroom

people.name: Isidro Ramón Antonio Ayora Cueva
people.nameZh: 伊西德羅·阿約拉·庫埃瓦

body.zh-Hant: 德國國家圖書館權威檔記載，伊西德羅·阿約拉·庫埃瓦生於1879年8月31日，出生地為厄瓜多爾的洛哈，卒於1978年3月22日，卒地為美國加州洛杉磯。美國國會圖書館人名權威檔以「Ayora, Isidro, 1879-1978」為款目，並收有「Ayora Cueva」的異稱。
body.en: The German National Library authority record gives Isidro Ayora Cueva's birth on 31 August 1879 at Loja, Ecuador, and his death on 22 March 1978 in Los Angeles, California. The Library of Congress name authority uses "Ayora, Isidro, 1879-1978" as the heading and lists the variant "Ayora Cueva".

body.zh-Hant: 權威檔的職業欄列有外科醫生、政治人物與總統，學位欄註明「Prof. Dr.」。簡註寫他是醫生、外科醫生，並註記1931年任厄瓜多爾總統。
body.en: The authority record lists his occupations as surgeon, politician and president, and gives the academic degree "Prof. Dr.". Its short note describes him as a physician and surgeon and records that he was President of Ecuador in 1931.

body.zh-Hant: 條目寫道，他生於洛哈，在基多學醫，到柏林做研究生階段的進修，並在德勒斯登完成實習。他在1909年回到厄瓜多爾後開設私人診所，並在中央大學教授產科，1917年接任產科主任（director of maternity）。
body.en: The entry says he was born in Loja, studied medicine in Quito, did postgraduate work in Berlin and completed an internship in Dresden. After returning to Ecuador in 1909 he built a private practice and taught obstetrics at Central University, where he became director of maternity in 1917.

citations.quote: Born in Loja, Ayora studied medicine in Quito
developed a private practice and taught obstetrics at Central University

heading.zh-Hant: 地方與大學職務、進入臨時政府
heading.en: Local and university posts, entry into the provisional government

body.zh-Hant: 條目記載，他在1916年當選洛哈代表，並擔任1924至1925年的縣（cantonal）議會議長。1925年他被任命為中央大學校長兼基多市民醫院院長。1926年1月10日他成為臨時執政委員會成員，兼任社會福利、勞工與農業部長；同年4月1日接受臨時總統一職。
body.en: The entry records that he was elected deputy of Loja in 1916 and was president of the cantonal council for 1924-1925. In 1925 he was appointed rector of Central University and director of the Civil Hospital of Quito. On 10 January 1926 he joined the provisional governing junta as minister of social welfare, labor and agriculture, and on 1 April 1926 he accepted the post of provisional president.

citations.quote: president of the cantonal council for 1924–1925
director of the Civil Hospital of Quito in 1925
On 10 January 1926 he became a member of the provisional governing junta
minister of social welfare , labor, and agriculture
On 1 April 1926 he accepted the position of provisional president

body.zh-Hant: 條目稱，他與普林斯頓經濟學者凱默勒（Edwin W. Kemmerer）訂約，由其率領顧問使節團，替國家財政問題提出對策；使節團於1926年10月擬定了法案。在軍方支持下，他得以施行使節團所提的大部分改革。他在1929年當選總統，但政策招致愈來愈多批評；基多爆發群眾示威後，他於1931年8月24日辭職，回到醫療工作。
body.en: The entry states that he concluded an agreement with the Princeton economist Edwin W. Kemmerer to head an advisory mission on the nation's financial problems; in October 1926 the mission drafted laws. With military backing he enacted most of the proposed reforms. He was elected to the presidency in 1929 but faced growing criticism for his policies; after mass demonstrations in Quito he resigned on 24 August 1931 and returned to his medical practice.

citations.quote: concluded an agreement with Princeton economist Edwin W. Kemmerer
propose solutions to the nation's financial problems
In October 1926 the mission drafted laws
with the backing of the military
was able to enact most of the sweeping reforms proposed
